metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Colombia agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is good to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Hi Kim, have you thought about when we should hold our joint meeting? I was thinking January 4th could be a good date. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: January 4th is a bit too soon, we just had holidays. How about January 10th? That gives us a bit more time to prepare and get back into work mode after the break.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: January 10th is okay, I guess. But I still think we could make January 4th work. We could just keep the meeting brief and to the point. By the way, what's your view on having the army play a role in governance?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don't think that's a good idea, having the army rule is bad. It's not a democratic way to govern and can lead to... well, let's just say it's not a path I think any country should take. January 4th is still too soon for me, can we stick with January 10th?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, as long as we're speaking the same language, people figure it out. Doesn't matter to me, with experience you can handle any situation. Live and let live, right? So, about the meeting, January 10th is still a bit late for me, how about we compromise on January 7th?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand what you're saying, but when it comes to the army ruling, it's not just about getting things done, it's about the principles of democracy. Having the army in charge undermines that. As for the meeting, January 7th is a bit better, but I still think we should aim for January 10th to ensure everyone is fully prepared.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: Principles of democracy are important, but so is stability and order. I think the army can provide that. In some cases, it's *necessary* for a country's progress. January 10th is still too late for me, can we at least send out a preliminary agenda by January 4th to get things moving?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I disagree, stability and order can be achieved without the army ruling. That's not a solution I can support. Sending out a preliminary agenda by January 4th might be okay, but let's not rush into anything without a solid plan. And I still think January 10th is a better date for the actual meeting.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I understand you don't support it, but I think it's worth considering. In China, we've seen it work in certain contexts. Maybe it's not for every country, but it's not entirely bad either. January 10th, okay, fine. But I'm sending out that preliminary agenda on January 4th, we need to get started.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand you think it's worth considering, but for me, having the army rule is bad, no matter the context. It's not something I can agree with. If you're sending out the agenda on January 4th, just make sure it's clear that it's preliminary and subject to change, so we don't confuse anyone. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance
